analysis.title: Rates Outlook 2027: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
key_insights: ING expects the US 10yr Treasury yield to rise to the 5.25%-plus area in the first quarter of 2027 (vs 4.9% currently), capped at 5.5%, then fall to 4.5-4.75% later in 2027 as inflation eases and the market re-discounts Fed cuts.

The three forces on long-end rates are the 'good' (AI-driven productivity growth), the 'bad' (elevated fiscal deficits) and the 'ugly' (renewed inflation from ongoing wars). AI is still about a fifth of the driver mix, but AI-related debt issuance pressure is rising and could eclipse the productivity effect in 2027.

ING says the February 2026 bond sell-off was sparked by the Iran war and elevated printed inflation. The market has not yet priced a material rate-cut process, so falling inflation later in 2027 is the main route to lower long-dated yields.

ING sees three routes to a 6% US 10yr yield: GDP growth of 3-4% lifting the real yield toward 4%, the fiscal deficit widening from the 6-6.5% range to 7-8%, or inflation staying near 3% or worsening (for example from a severe El Niño). ING does not forecast any of these.

ING would fade the tightening in US swap spreads. It expects the 10yr swap spread to widen back to 50bp-plus (now below 40bp) and the 30yr to 75bp at least, through 2027 or at least the first quarter. Treasury Secretary Bessent's long-end buybacks and fast-money longs in Treasuries paired with swap payers have tightened spreads.

A material cut to long-end Treasury issuance would dampen the fiscal-deficit pressure on yields. ING does not expect it and sees it as reserved for market stress, where de facto yield curve control might be an option.

Euro rates face near-term upside risk and a more constructive year-end. In the baseline the 2yr EUR swap rate falls about 50bp and the ECB terminal rate settles near 2.5% by end-2027. The 10yr swap rate stays sticky because of global supply. In the bad scenario it could go well above 4%, and in the benign one toward 2%.

For 2027 ING shifts its euro rates focus from oil to second-round inflation effects. Even with oil below $80/bbl in the baseline, swap rates would not get immediate relief. One bad inflation reading could repeat 2022-23, and ING sees limited downside to euro rates in 1H27.

Euro market pricing implies 1Y1Y inflation of 2.2% and 5Y5Y inflation swaps at 2.1%, which signals strong confidence in the ECB. An ECB forced to tolerate higher inflation (for example by French spread stress halting QT) is an unpriced risk that would produce significantly steeper curves.

ING thinks markets have overshot in repricing the terminal ECB rate. A rate above 3% is hard to reconcile with the previous 1.75-2.25% range. The 10yr euro swap rate is near fair value against nominal growth expectations of 3.3%, which limits downside.

France is the key fault line for European spreads. ING sees the 10yr OAT-Bund spread at about 150bp as a floor during electoral uncertainty and a possible move beyond 200bp if far-left support grows. Spreads could stay above 100bp even after the elections. ING says the market prices France as if it were already rated BBB.

French political and ratings calendar: Moody's affirmed France's last AA rating with a negative outlook, Fitch cut its outlook on A+ to negative, and the presidential election rounds are 18 April and 2 May 2027. Marine Le Pen could call snap legislative elections in the summer.

Germany's Bund safe-haven premium is temporary. ING expects the 10yr Bund to cheapen from about 13bp to at least 20bp over OIS. German gross bond funding could exceed €400bn next year, about €50bn more than this year, and ECB run-off adds at least another €80bn for the private sector to absorb.

ING expects the ECB to let market forces work while the turmoil is confined to France. Its tools, in escalating order, are a less hawkish stance, suspending QT by resuming reinvestments, and the TPI. The bar for intervention is high. The ECB's 2011 SMP intervention came with BTP-Bund spreads beyond 500bp.

ING expects lower GBP rates in 2027 but a delayed, volatile path. Markets price at least 100bp of Bank of England hikes (terminal rate around 4.75%), which ING disagrees with. The bigger dovish repricing comes in 2H27 once inflation nears 2% by end-2027, and a material term premium remains justified.

The 10yr GBP swap rate is explained about 98% by Bank of England expectations and the US swap curve (10yr level and 2s10s slope). A US 10yr swap rate move toward 6% would spill into sterling. Gilt supply is increasingly absorbed by price-sensitive foreign investors and other financials.

Dutch pension reforms peak in January 2027, with about €900bn of assets transitioning after about €600bn in 2026. ING expects limited market impact because funding ratios are healthy (ABP above 130%). The lasting effect is more frequent swap rebalancing as hedges track asset prices, and a structurally steeper 10s30s euro swap curve that depends on macro first.

macro_indicators.reading: 5.25%-plus in 1Q27, up to 5.5% cap, then 4.5-4.75% later in 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: ING expects upward pressure from AI issuance, deficits and sticky inflation early in 2027, then a decline as inflation falls and Fed cuts are repriced.
Current level cited as the starting point for the forecast move to 5.25%-plus.
ING expects re-widening as the tightening from Treasury buybacks and fast-money positioning is faded. The 30yr is targeted at 75bp at least.
A deficit that stays stable keeps debt dynamics a concern without escalation. A move to 7-8% would be a route to a 6% 10yr yield.
Real yield is the key driver of the nominal yield. A rise toward 4% would take the 10yr Treasury yield to 6%.
Reflects a repricing of the ECB path if inflation eases. Upside risk of another 100bp if inflation surprises and policy transmission looks weaker.

macro_indicators.reading: well above 4% in adverse case, toward 2% in fast disinflation
macro_indicators.interpretation: Sticky at elevated levels in the baseline because of global bond supply.
ING thinks the market has overshot with a terminal rate above 3%.
Signals strong market confidence in the ECB and is consistent with pricing three further ECB hikes.
Little priced risk to the ECB's 2% commitment, so an ECB forced to tolerate inflation is an unpriced risk.
A political risk premium persists until a credible French fiscal consolidation path appears.
Safe-haven richness fades while German supply increases.

macro_indicators.indicator: Bank of England terminal rate priced by markets
macro_indicators.interpretation: ING disagrees and sees the pricing as a risk premium from past dovish-positioning losses.
About €50bn more than this year. Net issuance rises about half as much because of higher redemptions.

trade_ideas.description: Fade the tightening in US swap spreads: position for 10yr swap spread widening to 50bp-plus and 30yr to 75bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Spreads are tight because of Treasury buybacks and fast-money positioning, and ING expects re-widening pressure through 2027 or at least 1Q27.
trade_ideas.risk: An aggressive Treasury decision to cancel some long-end auctions or add to buybacks.

trade_ideas.description: Avoid bond-bullish positioning early in 2027 and stay bearish Treasuries into 1Q27, with a bullish tilt later as inflation falls
trade_ideas.rationale: Inflation, deficits and AI issuance push the 10yr toward 5.25-5.5% before inflation falls and Fed cuts are repriced.
trade_ideas.risk: A material cut to long-end Treasury funding or a market stress event could lower yields sooner.

risk_factors: Inflation not easing enough, with US inflation sticky near 3% or worse (for example from a severe El Niño), which is a route to a 6% 10yr Treasury yield.
US fiscal deficit worsening from 6-6.5% to 7-8%.
US GDP growth of 3-4%, which would lift the real yield toward 4%.
AI-related debt issuance crowding out the productivity benefit.
Second-round inflation effects in the euro area, and an ECB unable to stem inflation or forced to tolerate it.
French fiscal and political risk, further sovereign rating downgrades, and foreign investors leaving French bonds.
Weaker perceived transmission of monetary policy, which could push 2yr euro swap rates another 100bp higher.
Global bond supply from government debt, quantitative tightening and possible private-sector borrowing.
Price-sensitive buyers of gilts, which adds volatility to the gilt market.
Unexpected Treasury policy changes on long-end issuance.
vol_and_positioning: Fast-money players are long Treasuries and paying fixed in swaps against an implied cap on swap spreads, which has tightened US swap spreads.
Foreign investors and other financials (asset managers, hedge funds) are absorbing the increase in gilt supply and may sell quickly if gilts look less attractive.
Japanese investors have shown sensitivity to French election risk in the past, though data through August show no larger shift out of French bonds.
Dutch pension funds will rebalance interest rate hedges more frequently as hedging becomes tied to asset prices, which creates recurring swap flows.
geopolitical: The Iran war sparked the February 2026 bond sell-off and the oil price surge, and ongoing wars keep inflation pressure in focus.
French politics: 2027 presidential election on 18 April and 2 May, with possible snap legislative elections in summer if Marine Le Pen wins, and tail risk of far-left Jean-Luc Mélenchon support.

Spain holds elections later this month, Italy must hold legislative elections before the end of 2027, Finland holds parliamentary elections, and Germany faces five state elections (four in April-May, one in September).
Energy prices remain unsettled and the global geopolitical landscape is unstable.

tension_points.bull_case: Falling inflation later in 2027 lets the Fed step away and the market re-discount cuts, taking the 10yr to 4.5-4.75%.
tension_points.bear_case: Sticky inflation near 3%, a wider deficit or 3-4% GDP growth could push the 10yr to 6%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation staying near 3% and not falling, the fiscal deficit moving to 7-8%, or GDP growth reaching 3-4%.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation pressures ease and the ECB terminal rate anchors near 2.5%, taking the 2yr EUR swap rate down about 50bp and the 10yr toward 2% in the fast-disinflation case.
tension_points.bear_case: Second-round inflation effects could push the 10yr swap rate well above 4% and the 2yr up another 100bp.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A series of upside inflation surprises, or an ECB forced to tolerate higher inflation because of French spread stress.

tension_points.bull_case: A 2027 budget with some consolidation passes, or a Le Pen win delivers fiscal consolidation, returning spreads toward pre-September levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Unrealistic consolidation plans, a hung parliament and far-left gains push the OAT-Bund spread beyond 200bp and invite more downgrades.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A credible multi-year French consolidation plan would remove the premium, while a greater probability of far-left policies such as cancelling French debt held by the Bank of France would push spreads beyond 200bp.
